rationale:
All candidates are direct matches for abdominal aortic aneurysm by trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, so selection hinges on PRS-comparable performance evidence, covariate cleanliness, and structural/model-quality signals.

PGS001784 is preferred because it is the only candidate with an explicit PRS-comparable metric (Nagelkerke’s R² with covariates regressed out = 0.014661) in a large European evaluation sample (n=350,767), and it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS-auto) with very broad variant coverage (911,440). Its covariates are standard demographic + PCs (age/sex terms and 20 PCs), which is not strong clinical leakage.

Alternatives are weaker on the visible evidence: PGS000753 is very sparse (29 variants, P+T) despite a moderate OR=1.37; PGS002054 has only a partial correlation (~0.0144) and comes from a portability benchmarking study; PGS003429/PGS003972/PGS003973 report only full-model AUROC/C-index with unknown or basic covariates, making their discrimination less comparable to PRS-only performance.

Heritability records available are only approximate matches (aortic aneurysm/dissection) with low/unstable h2 estimates, so they do not provide a strong ceiling check here; nonetheless, the reported PRS-only R² for PGS001784 is modest and plausible rather than suggestive of covariate-driven inflation.

Confidence is Moderate because several candidates lack PRS-only metrics (so direct PRS-to-PRS comparability is limited), and some reported full-model AUROCs (e.g., 0.882) cannot be fairly compared without PRS-only decomposition.

Target trait is alcohol dependence. Direct-match candidates are those with trait_efo alcohol dependence and phenotyping_reported alcohol use disorder: PGS002738 and PGS002739 (PGS000201/PGS000202 are labeled problematic alcohol use, though their phenotyping is also AUD criteria count). PGS002738 is preferred because it is evaluated in Europeans (n=7,900) matching the typical deployment/benchmark context implied by the other EUR-evaluated candidates, and it reports a reasonably strong discrimination-style effect size (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96, 95% CI 1.54–2.51), which is more directly interpretable for case/control risk stratification than the small incremental ΔR² values reported for PGS000201/PGS000202. PGS002739 is evaluated only in African American/Afro-Caribbean samples (n=6,315) and is gene-based with very low variant count (858), making it less comparable/portable to the EUR-focused candidate set here. Confidence is not High because none of the candidates report clean PRS-only AUC or PRS-only R², covariates are unknown for PGS002738, and the available heritability estimates for alcohol dependence are modest (h2 ~0.10 observed; liability ~0.18), limiting expectations for large PRS-only R².
